title: Ethiopian Cracked Wheat
community: All of Ethiopia — the simple nourishing porridge
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Kinche — cracked wheat or barley simmered until completely soft, drained, and dressed with kibbeh and a pinch of berbere or mitmita. The nourishing everyday porridge of Ethiopian households — quick, filling, and elevated by the addition of spiced clarified butter.
longDesc: Kinche is the unpretentious daily porridge of Ethiopia — cracked wheat or barley, simply boiled until tender, then transformed by a spoonful of kibbeh. It is eaten for breakfast across the highlands, particularly during fasting periods when richer foods are not consumed.
ingredients: 1.5 cups cracked wheat (freekeh) or cracked barley
steps: Bring water to a boil. Add salt and grain.
Simmer covered 20—25 minutes until completely tender.
Most water should be absorbed. Drain any excess.
Add a generous spoonful of kibbeh in the centre.
chefTips: Kinche should be tender but still have some texture — not mushy.
The kibbeh added at the end is what makes kinche kinche.
cookingScience: See ETH009 for barley cooking science.
sustainabilityTips: Cracked wheat and barley are affordable, locally grown Ethiopian grains.
servedWith: During fasting period as a fasting meal (without kibbeh)
storage: Refrigerate 3 days. Reheat with a splash of water.
culturalNote: Kinche is the fasting food of Ethiopia's Orthodox Christian majority — during the 250+ annual fasting days, when animal products are avoided, kinche dressed with plant-based oil rather than kibbeh becomes the morning meal that sustains the faithful through the long days of prayer.
